headline: State Minister Ishraque drew licensed gun in self-defence during anti-drug drive
summary: Ishraque Hossain claims he used his firearm to deter a threatening crowd during an operation in Gandaria, while DMP orders a probe into the incident.
details: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain has defended his actions after being seen with a firearm during an 'anti-drug operation' in Gandaria, Dhaka.
In a statement, the Dhaka-6 MP said he and his security personnel drew their licensed weapons briefly when 30 to 35 people advanced toward their motorcade in a threatening manner.
Ishraque claimed law enforcement had warned him of possible attacks, including gunfire from rooftops, before the operation began.
The minister accused several media outlets of distorted reporting for focusing on images of him holding a gun while ignoring the operation's results.
According to the statement, the operation dismantled four to five illegal drug dens and led to the detention of six suspected drug traders.
Authorities also seized heroin or heroin-like substances, foreign liquor, drug-use paraphernalia, sharp weapons, and stolen mobile phones.
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has ordered a probe into the display of firearms during the drive, according to reports.
Ishraque reiterated the government's zero-tolerance policy on drugs and committed to making Dhaka-6 drug-free.
caption:
A State Minister drew his gun during an anti-drug drive in Dhaka. He says it was for self-defence—the police are now probing.

State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain has defended his actions after being seen with a firearm during an 'anti-drug operation' in Gandaria, Dhaka.

In a statement, the Dhaka-6 MP said he and his security personnel drew their licensed weapons briefly when 30 to 35 people advanced toward their motorcade in a threatening manner.

Ishraque claimed law enforcement had warned him of possible attacks, including gunfire from rooftops, before the operation began.

The minister accused several media outlets of distorted reporting for focusing on images of him holding a gun while ignoring the operation's results.

According to the statement, the operation dismantled four to five illegal drug dens and led to the detention of six suspected drug traders.

Authorities also seized heroin or heroin-like substances, foreign liquor, drug-use paraphernalia, sharp weapons, and stolen mobile phones.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has ordered a probe into the display of firearms during the drive, according to reports.

Ishraque reiterated the government's zero-tolerance policy on drugs and committed to making Dhaka-6 drug-free.

headline: 6 deaths in 24 hours as dengue cases surge in Bangladesh
summary: Over 2,800 patients were admitted to hospitals nationwide in a single day, bringing the yearly death toll to 348.
details: Six people died from dengue fever in the last 24 hours, according to a press release from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) issued on Sunday.
During the same period, 2,888 patients were admitted to various hospitals across the country due to dengue infections.
The breakdown of admissions includes 595 in the Dhaka division (outside city corporations), 232 in Dhaka North City Corporation, and 231 in Dhaka South City Corporation.
Other regional admissions include 290 in Khulna, 200 in Rajshahi, 199 in Barishal, 161 in Chattogram, 93 in Mymensingh, 72 in Rangpur, and 15 in Sylhet.
This brings the total number of dengue-related deaths this year to 348, with 112,400 patients admitted to hospitals so far in 2024.
caption:
6 deaths and nearly 2,900 hospitalizations in just 24 hours.

Six people died from dengue fever in the last 24 hours, according to a press release from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) issued on Sunday.

During the same period, 2,888 patients were admitted to various hospitals across the country due to dengue infections.

The breakdown of admissions includes 595 in the Dhaka division (outside city corporations), 232 in Dhaka North City Corporation, and 231 in Dhaka South City Corporation.

Other regional admissions include 290 in Khulna, 200 in Rajshahi, 199 in Barishal, 161 in Chattogram, 93 in Mymensingh, 72 in Rangpur, and 15 in Sylhet.

This brings the total number of dengue-related deaths this year to 348, with 112,400 patients admitted to hospitals so far in 2024.
